If the same current is passed in both, the ratio of the magnetic field at the centre of the loop  \left({B}_{L}\right)$ to that at the centre of the coil \left({B}_{C}\right),$ i.e. $\dfrac{{B}_{L}}{{B}_{C}} will be$

questions.q: An electron is moving along& $+ x$ direction with a velocity of~$6 \times {10}^{6}\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm{ms}^{-1}$. It enters a region of uniform electric field of $300V / cm$ pointing along~$+ y$ direction. The magnitude and direction of the magnetic field set up in this region such that the electron keeps moving along the x direction will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$q ∨ B = qE$

$B = \dfrac{E}{V} = \dfrac{30000}{6 \times {10}^{6}} = 5 \times {10}^{3}T$

Magnetic force~$F = q ( \overset{→}{V} \times \overset{→}{B} )$

So Ans.$5 \times {10}^{3}T$& ,along +Z direction

questions.q: A charge $Q$ is moving $d\overset{→}{l}$ distance in the magnetic field $\overset{→}{B}$. Find the value of work done by $\overset{→}{B}$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Since force on a point charge by magnetic field is always perpendicular to& $\overset{→}{v} \left[\overset{→}{F} =q \left(\overset{→}{v} \times \overset{→}{B}\right)\right]

$∴$ Work by magnetic force on the point charge is zero.

$

questions.q:
The magnitude of magnetic induction at mid-point $O$ due to current arrangement as shown in figure& will be

.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The magnetic field at point $O$~due to the two semi-infinite portions of both wires lying along line $BE$ will be $0$.

Using right-hand rule, it can be determined that the magnetic field due to both the semi-infinite portions of wires $BC\text{and}ET$~which are perpendicular to $BE$ will be outwards from the plane.

The magnetic field due to one such portion will be:

$B = \dfrac{{μ}_{0}I}{4\pi\left(\dfrac{a}{2}\right)}$

Since the magnetic field of both the portions is in same direction, the net magnetic field at $O$ will be:

${B}_{net} = 2 \times \dfrac{{μ}_{0}I}{4\pi\left(\dfrac{a}{2}\right)} = \dfrac{{μ}_{0}I}{\pia}$

questions.q: A proton and an alpha particle of the same velocity enter in a uniform magnetic field which is acting perpendicular to their direction of motion. The ratio of the radii of the circular paths described by the alpha particle and proton is&
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Radius of circular path of charged particle& \left(q\right)$~of mass~ \left(m\right)$~moving with velocity~ \left(v\right)$ in magnetic field \left(B\right)$~is given by~$r = \dfrac{mv}{qB}$

$\dfrac{r\alpha}{rp} = \dfrac{\dfrac{\left(4m\right)v}{\left(2e\right)B}}{\dfrac{mv}{eB}} = 2: 1$

questions.q: A rigid square loop of side $‘a’$ and carrying current ${I}_{2}$ is lying on a horizontal surface near a long current ${I}_{1}$ carrying wire in the same plane as shown in figure. The net force on the loop due to the wire will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Force on segment 1-2 and 3-4 will get cancel out.
Force on segment 4-1,
${F}_{1} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}{I}_{1}{I}_{2}}{2\pia} \times a$ toward Right
Force on segment 2-3:
${F}_{2} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}{I}_{1}{I}_{2}}{2\pi ( 2a )} \times a$ toward left
Net force on loop:
${F}_{net} = {F}_{1} - {F}_{2}$ toward Right
$= \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}{I}_{1}{I}_{2}}{2\pi} - \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}{I}_{1}{I}_{2}}{4\pi}$
$= \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}{I}_{1}{I}_{2}}{4\pi}$ toward Right or repulsive

questions.q: Magnitude of magnetic field (in SI units) at the centre of a hexagonal shape coil of side& $10cm, 50$ turns and carrying current$I$~ (Ampere) in units of~$\dfrac{{μ}_{0}I}{π}$ is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The magnetic field due to the current-carrying finite length wire is given by

$B = \dfrac{{μ}_{0}I}{4\piR} \left[sin{θ}_{1} + sin{θ}_{2}\right]$

Here for hexagonal shape coil,~${θ}_{1} = {θ}_{2} = 30 °$.

So, the net magnetic field at the centre~will be~$B = 50 \times6 \times $\dfrac{{μ}_{0}i}{4\pi $\$left(\dfrac{10}{100}$cos30 °\right)} \left[sin30 ° + sin30 °\right]$

$B = 2 \times 75 \times 10\dfrac{{μ}_{0}i}{\sqrt{3}\pi} \left(\dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}\right)

$B = $\dfrac{1500}{3}\dfrac{{μ}_{0}i}{π} = \lleft(500\sqrt{3}\right)\dfrac{{μ}_{0}i}{π}$

$

questions.q: Two charged particles, having same kinetic energy, are allowed to pass through a uniform magnetic field perpendicular to the direction of motion. If the ratio of radii of their circular paths is $6: 5$~and their respective masses ratio is $9: 4$. Then, the ratio of their charges will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Radius of charged particle moving in circular path $R = \dfrac{2mK}{qB}$, here,~$B$~is magnetic field and~$K$~is kinetic energy.

So,~$q = \dfrac{2mK}{RB}$

Now, ratio of the charges is~$\dfrac{q1}{q2} = \sqrt{\dfrac{m1}{m2}} \times \dfrac{R2}{R1} = \sqrt{\dfrac{9}{4}} \times \dfrac{5}{6} = \dfrac{5}{4}$

questions.q: In a co-axial straight cable, the central conductor and the outer conductor carry equal currents in opposite directions. The magnetic field is zero :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Since the current carried by the outer& and inner are equal and& in opposite direction, magnetic field produced by the cylinders at a point& P(distance& r from central axis) is

$⇒ \overset{→}{B}outer = \dfrac{\muo}{4\pi}i\dfrac{\overset{→}{dl} \times \overset{→}{r}}{r3}$

$⇒ \overset{→}{B}inner = - \dfrac{\muo}{4\pi}i\dfrac{\overset{→}{dl} \times \overset{→}{r}}{r3}$

$⇒ \overset{→}{B} = \overset{→}{B}outer + \overset{→}{B}inner = 0$

questions.q: In an experiment, electrons are accelerated, from rest, by applying a voltage of $500 \mathrm{~V}$. Calculate the radius of the path if a magnetic field $100 \mathrm{mT}$ is then applied. [Charge of the electron $=1.6 \times 10^{-19} \mathrm{C}$ Mass of the electron  \left.=9.1 \times 10^{-31} \mathrm{~kg}\right]$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: Radius of the path (r) is given by $\mathrm{r}=\frac{\mathrm{mv}}{\mathrm{qB}}\begin{aligned} \mathrm{r}$&=$\frac{\sqrt{2 \mathrm{mk}}}{\mathrm{eB}} \quad(\because \mathrm{p}=\mathrm{mv}=\sqrt{2 \mathrm{mk}})$\\ &=$\frac{\sqrt{2 \mathrm{meV}}}{\mathrm{eB}} \quad(\because \mathrm{k}=\mathrm{eV})$\\ $\mathrm{r}$&=$\frac{\sqrt{\frac{2 \mathrm{~m}}{\mathrm{e}} \mathrm{V}}}{\mathrm{B}}=\frac{\sqrt{\frac{2 \times 9.1 \times 10^{-31}}{1.6 \times 10^{-19}}(500)}}{100 \times 10^{-3}} \end{aligned}r=\frac{\sqrt{\frac{9.1}{0.16} \times 10^{-10}}}{10^{-1}}=\frac{3}{4} \times 10^{-4}=7.5 \times 10^{-4}$

questions.q: A long conducting wire having a current $I$ flowing through it, is bent into a circular coil of $N$ turns. Then it is bent into a circular coil of $n$ turns. The magnetic field is calculated at the centre of coils in both the cases. The ratio of the magnetic field in first case to that of second case is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As in both cases, length of the wire will remain the same, therefore

$l = \left(2\piR\right)N = \left(2\pir\right)n ⇒ \dfrac{R}{r} = \dfrac{n}{N}$

Now magnetic field due to single circular coil is given by,~$B = \left(\dfrac{{μ}_{0}I}{2r}\right).

Therefore, required ratio of total magnetic field wil be,

\dfrac{B1}{B2} = \dfrac{N $\$left(\dfrac{{μ}_{0}I}{2R}\rrright)}{n\$left(\dfrac{{μ}_{0}I}{2r}\right)} = \left(\dfrac{N2}{n2}\right)

questions.q:
A velocity selector consists of electric field $\overset{→}{E} = E\overset{^}{k}$ and magnetic field $\overset{→}{B} = B\overset{^}{j}$ with $B = 12mT$. The value $E$~required for an electron of energy $728$ eV moving along the positive $x$-axis to pass undeflected is~

(Given, mass of electron $= 9 . 1 \times {10}^{- 31}kg$)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Fiven that& $\overset{→}{E} = E\overset{^}{k}$~and~$\overset{→}{B} = 12\overset{^}{j}mT$

Kinetic energy$= 728eV$

Kinetic energy $= \dfrac{1}{2}mv^{2}$

$⇒ 728eV = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 9 . 1 \times {10}^{- 31} \times v^{2}$

$⇒ 728 \times 1 . 6 \times {10}^{- 19} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 9 . 1 \times {10}^{- 31} \times v^{2}$

$⇒ v = 16 \times {10}^{6}ms^{- 1}$

For electron to move undeflected~net force on it should be zero.

$⇒ eE = evB$

$⇒ E = vB = 16 \times {10}^{6} \times 12 \times {10}^{- 3}$

$⇒ E = 192 \times {10}^{3}Vm^{- 1} = 192kVm^{- 1}$

questions.q: Find the magnetic field at the point P in figure. The curved portion is a semicircle connected to two long straight wires.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Magnitude of magnetic field due to semi-infinite portion of wire AB at point C& is

${B}_{1} = \dfrac{{μ}_{0}i}{4\pir}$

Magnitude of magnetic field due to semicircular arc BD at point C~is

${B}_{2} = \dfrac{{μ}_{0}i}{4r}$

Magnitude of magnetic field due to semi-infinite portion~DE~at point C~is~0.

Using right-hand rule, it can be seen that directions of~$\overset{→}{B1}$~and~$\overset{→}{B2}$~are~both outwards from the plane.

Therefore, the magnitude of net magnetic field at point C is

$B = {B}_{1} + {B}_{2}$

~ ~$= \dfrac{{μ}_{0}i}{2r} \left[\dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{1}{2\pi}\right]

$

questions.q: A charged particle (mass& $m$~and charge $q$) moves along~$X$~axis with velocity~${V}_{0}$. When it passes through the origin it enters a region having uniform electric field~$\overset{→}{E} = - E\overset{^}{j}$~which extends upto~$x = d$. Equation of path of electron in the region~$x > d$& is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$x > d$path is straight line

$\dfrac{- y - \dfrac{1}{2}at^{2}}{x - d} = \dfrac{at}{V0}$

$\dfrac{- y - \dfrac{1}{2}at^{2}}{at} = \dfrac{x - d}{V0}$

$\dfrac{- y}{at} - \dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{d}{V0} = \dfrac{x}{V0} - \dfrac{d}{V0}$

$\dfrac{- my{V}_{0}}{qEd} = \dfrac{x}{V0} - \dfrac{d}{2{V}_{0}}$

$y = \dfrac{- qEd}{m{V}_{0}} \left(\dfrac{x}{V0} - \dfrac{d}{2{V}_{0}}\right)

$y = $\dfrac{qEd}{m{V}_{0}^{2}} \left(\dfrac{d}{2} -$x\right)$.

$

questions.solution: Every part ($dl$ ) of the wire is pulled by the force $i ( dl ) B$ acting perpendicular to the current $ \text{ and } $& magnetic field giving it the shape of a circle.

questions.q: A charge particle is moving in a uniform magnetic field \left(2\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j}\right)T$. If it has an acceleration of \left(\alpha\overset{^}{i} - 4\overset{^}{j}\right)ms^{- 2}$, then the value of $\alpha$ will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given that uniform magnetic field, $\vec{B}=(2 \hat{i}+3 \hat{j}) T$
Acceleration $\vec{a}=(\alpha \hat{i}-4 \hat{j}) \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s}^2$ We know that
$F=q(\vec{v} \times \vec{B}) \Rightarrow m \vec{a}=q(\vec{v} \times \vec{B})$
Here, $\vec{a} \perp \vec{B}$, so, $\vec{a} \cdot \vec{B}=0$
$(\alpha \hat{i}-4 \hat{j})(2 \hat{i}+3 \hat{j})=0 \Rightarrow 2 \alpha-12=0 \Rightarrow \alpha=6$

questions.q: A proton and an $\alpha$- particle (with their masses in the ratio of $1: 4$ and charges in the ratio of $1: 2$ ) are accelerated from rest through a potential difference $V .$ If a uniform magnetic field  \left(B\right)$ is set up perpendicular to their velocities, the ratio of the radii ${r}_{p}: {r}_{\alpha}$ of the circular paths described by them will be:$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The kinetic energy of a charge& $q$~of mass~$m$~in potential is given by,

$\dfrac{1}{2}mv^{2} = qV$

$mv = \sqrt{2mqV}$

Then, the radius of the charge will be,

$r = \dfrac{2mqV}{qB}$

$⇒ r ∝ \sqrt{\dfrac{m}{q}}$

Hence, the ratio of radius of proton to~$\alpha$-particle,

$\dfrac{{r}_{p}}{{r}_{\alpha}} =\sqrt{\dfrac{1}{4} \times \dfrac{2}{1}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$.

questions.q: A very long wire ABDMNDC is shown in figure carrying current I. AB and BC parts are straight, long and at right angle. At D wire forms a circular turn DMND of radius R. AB, BC parts are tangential to circular turn at N and D. Magnetic filed at the center of circle is:

questions.solution:
$\overset{→}{{B}_{0}} = {\left(\overset{→}{{B}_{0}}\right)}_{1} + {\left(\overset{→}{{B}_{0}}\right)}_{2} + {\left(\overset{→}{{B}_{0}}\right)}_{3} + {\left(\overset{→}{{B}_{0}}\right)}_{4}$
$\dfrac{{\mu}_{0}i}{4\piR}\left[sin ⁡ 90 ° - sin45 °\right]⨂ + \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}i}{2R}⨀ +\dfrac{{\mu}_{0}i}{4\piR} ( sin45 ° + sin90 ° ) ⨀$
$- \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}i}{4\piR}\left[1 - \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right] + \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}i}{2R} + \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}i}{4\piR}\left[\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} + 1\right]⨀$
$= \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}i}{4\piR}\left[- 1 + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} + 2\pi + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} + 1\right]⨀ = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}i}{4\piR}\left[\sqrt{2} + 2\pi\right]⨀ = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}i}{2\piR}\left[\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} + \pi\right]⨀$

We know, $r = \dfrac{mv}{qB} \left(∵ \text{K.E.$=}\dfrac{1}{2}mv^{2}\right)$

The magnitude of $B$ is _____\times 10^{-1} \mathrm{~T}$ (given, $\mathrm{g}=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2 ).

questions.q: The ratio of magnetic field at the centre of a current carrying coil of radius $r$~to the magnetic field at distance $r$ from the centre of coil on its axis is $\sqrt{x}: 1$. The value of $x$ is _____.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the magnetic field at any axial point situated at a distance& $x$~from the centre of a circular current carrying conductor of radius~$r$~can be written as

$B = \dfrac{{μ}_{0}Ir^{2}}{2 \left(r^{2} + x^{2}\right)3 / 2} . . . \left($1\right)$

Substitute~$0$~for~$x$~in~equation (1) to calculate the magnetic field~\left({B}_{c}\right)~at the centre of the conductor.

\begin{cases}{B}_{c}$ \text{ and } = \text{ and } $\dfrac{{μ}_{0}Ir^{2}}{2\left(r^{2} + {0}^{2}\right)3 / 2}$\\ \text{ and } = \text{ and } $\dfrac{{μ}_{0}Ir^{2}}{2r^{3}}$\\ \text{ and } = \text{ and } $\dfrac{{μ}_{0}I}{2r} . . . \left($2\right)\end{cases}$

Substitute~$r$ for $x$~in~equation (1) to calculate the magnetic field~\left({B}_{r}\right)at the given distance from the centre of the conductor.

\begin{cases}{B}_{r}$ \text{ and } = \text{ and } $\dfrac{{μ}_{0}Ir^{2}}{2\left(r^{2} + r^{2}\right)3 / 2}$\\ \text{ and } = \text{ and } $\dfrac{{μ}_{0}Ir^{2}}{4\sqrt{2}r^{3}}$\\ \text{ and } = \text{ and } $\dfrac{{μ}_{0}I}{4\sqrt{2}r} . . . \left($3\right)\end{cases}$

Divide equation (2) by equation (3) to calculate the required ratio of the magnetic fields.

\begin{cases}\dfrac{Bc}{Br}$ \text{ and } = \text{ and } $\dfrac{{μ}_{0}I2r}{{μ}_{0}I4\sqrt{2}r}$\\ \text{ and } = \text{ and } $2\sqrt{2}$\\ \text{ and } = \text{ and } $\sqrt{8}\end{cases}

$

questions.q: A deuteron and a proton moving with equal kinetic energy enter into to a uniform magnetic field at right angle to the field. If ${r}_{d}$~and ${r}_{p}$ are the radii of their circular paths respectively, then the ratio $\dfrac{rd}{rp}$ will be $\sqrt{x}: 1$~where $x$ is _____ .
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As we know, radius of circular path followed by charged particle under perpendicular magnetic field is given by,

$R = \dfrac{mv}{qB}$~and~$KE = \dfrac{1}{2}mv^{2}$

Therefore,

$⇒ R = \dfrac{2m\left(KE\right)}{qB}$~ Then,~$R ∝ \dfrac{m}{q}$

$⇒ \dfrac{Rd}{Rp} = \sqrt{\dfrac{md}{mp}} \times \dfrac{qp}{qd} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2}{1}} \times \dfrac{1}{1} = \sqrt{2}: 1$

Thus,~$x = 2$.

questions.q: A current of 5A exists in a square loop of side $\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \mathrm{~m}$. Then the magnitude of the magnetic field $B$ at the centre of the square loop will be $p \times 10^{-6} \mathrm{~T}$. where, value of p is _____ .  \left[\right.$ Take \left.\mu_0=4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \mathrm{TmA}^{-1}\right].$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: Let B be the magnetic field due to single side $\begin{aligned} & \text { then } B=\frac{\mu_0 \mathrm{i}}{4 \pi \mathrm{~d}}\left(\sin \theta_1+\sin \theta_2\right) \\ & =\frac{10^{-7} \times 5 \times 2}{\frac{1}{2 \sqrt{2}}} \times \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}=2 \times 10^{-6} \\ & \therefore B_{\text {net }} \text { at centre } O=4 B \\ & =8 \times 10^{-6} \end{aligned}$

questions.q: The horizontal component of earth's magnetic field at a place is $3 . 5 \times {10}^{- 5}T$. A very long straight conductor carrying current of $\sqrt{2}A$ in the direction from South east to North West is placed. The force per unit length experienced by the conductor is ________\times {10}^{- 6}Nm^{- 1}.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Horizontal component of magnetic field, ${B}_{H} = 3 . 5 \times {10}^{- 5}T$

Force acting on wire, $F = ilBsin\theta, \text{where}i = \sqrt{2}A$

Therefore, $\dfrac{F}{l} = iBsin\theta = \sqrt{2} \times 3 . 5 \times {10}^{- 5} \times \dfrac{1}{2}$

$= 35 \times {10}^{- 6}Nm^{- 1}$
